extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, patent practitioners, inventors, and informed scientific/industrial readership interested in patent law and policy (particularly British patent law)
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and normative recommendations concerning the British patent system (history, legal doctrines, administrative practice) with proposed criteria for patent validity, working, disclosure, and national policy. Focuses on how patent law should be structured to serve national industrial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity conditional on filing of specification enabling skilled artisan
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent grant was made in consideration of the filing by the patentee of such a description of his invention as would enable a skilled artisan in the trade to work the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lord Mansfield laid down that the validity of patents is conditional upon their compliance with this standard of disclosure; this doctrine evolved into the modern patent specification requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'True and first inventor' construed in modern sense (specification doctrine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting the Statute of Monopolies by the contemporary meaning of its language, the Courts construed the phrase 'true and first inventor' in its modern sense, investing the inventor with rights without any corresponding obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This judicial construction left the Statute 'devoid of any expressed consideration' and led to the development of the patent specification doctrine emphasizing disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty standard shifted from practice to disclosure within the realm
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision involved the shifting of novelty from the practice of the trade to novelty of disclosure within the realm, i.e. novelty of what has been disclosed/published within the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shift depressed commercial value of patents and discouraged importation of industries not practiced within the realm, because disclosure-based novelty raised an uneconomic and impracticable standard of novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official examination (50 years' search) reduces monopoly power/value
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1905 a fifty years' search through British patent specifications came into operation; the effect of official examination is always to reduce the restraining power of a monopoly in a degree corresponding with the extent of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official examination can reduce many grants to the level of commercial advertisement; when conducted through specifications of lapsed patents it further undercuts the value of patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal/'rounding off' clause excluding lapsed specifications from public knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Framers introduced at the last moment a clause to 'round off' the official search by removing British patent specifications not retained on or included in the official files from the stock of public knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because removed specifications cannot be cited as evidence of prior anticipation, the Commonwealth standard was sacrificed to official convenience, permitting valid patents even where disclosure identical with earlier publication exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working (commercial exploitation) as a criterion of patent value and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patents Act of 1919 explicitly reaffirms the doctrine of the old Law as to 'working'; the writer argues that on proof of commercial working the validity of a patent should be freed from attack by proof of prior publication within the realm, and the patent freed from the payment of further renewal fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting relief and security upon proof of commercial working would make law and practice consistent, effective, and economical, reduce administration cost and delays, and secure broad claims once the patent is reduced to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent law should serve national and competitive policy rather than international uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The favourable treatment of the inventor cannot be based upon international principles. It is part and parcel of a purely national and competitive policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All considerations of international or imperial comity should be subordinated to the national interest; protection to the importer of a new industry is a national competitive instrument and should not be sacrificed for imperial uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: The inventor's services should be competed for by offering widest compatible security
rubrics_metrics.description: The services of the inventor should be competed for by offering him the widest security for his monopoly compatible with the state of the national industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical measures suggested include freeing patents from attacks based on prior realm publication upon proof of commercial working and waiving further renewal fees to secure inventor services and encourage importation/introduction of industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current law needs a clear, business-like statement of principles and administrative coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The law obviously stands in need of a clear and business-like statement of its principles; successive modifications have left the system without claim to industrial value, consistency, or administrative economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An inquiry into the working of the system is warranted to bring administrative practice into harmony with legal requirements, and to adopt reforms requiring courage and conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative examination practice should not undercut novelty or patent value
rubrics_metrics.description: If official examination is conducted through specifications of lapsed patents, the effect is to reduce the restraining power and commercial value of patents; removal of older specifications from public stock further distorts novelty law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any official search/examination regime must be designed so as not to enable valid patents despite identical prior disclosure, and must balance public knowledge with patentee protection to preserve industrial incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent litigation as an acceptable (even healthy) consequence of firmer patent protection
rubrics_metrics.description: There would, no doubt, be some increase in litigation, but patent litigation is a sign of healthy progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting increased litigation is part of the proposed reform trade-off to secure clearer, stronger patent rights that better serve industrial progress.
